Windows PE DF 53.16 workshop task chooser source grammar

Configured source images: native-pe-images.json reference and classic.
pe-functions.tsv retains image identity, SHA-256, original complete unwind
owners and all chained ranges. pe-*.asm, pe-branches.tsv, pe-conditions.tsv,
pe-switches.tsv and pe-virtuals.tsv retain original machine text and control
flow. pe-ghidra-functions.tsv names actual decompiled bodies. The full native
building-sheet renderer remains in assembly; its complete chooser arm is
exported separately as task-choice-render-branch. Other building panels are
outside this chooser arm. This is offline source extraction, not an observed
in-game rendering result.
pe-vtables.tsv binds the four actual candidate constructors to every virtual
slot through +0x68, including all title, requirement, additional and color
suppliers. The chooser's exits into other building panels are call-shaped in
Ghidra C; pe-branches.tsv retains the unmodified conditional/target edges.

Native fields, reference / classic return RVAs:
  Title        0x185443 / 0x1853d3
  Requirement  0x185597 / 0x185527
  Additional   0x185690 / 0x185620
Each field has one native addst call, width 0. No separate upper/lower font
call occurs in this branch. Candidate vtable +0x08 formats Title; +0x58 gives
Requirement; +0x60 gives Additional; +0x68 selects Additional color. A nonempty
Requirement has priority and is red. Empty fields produce no annotation.
Title is locally clipped and gets an ellipsis before addst. The original
candidate and formatter remain in this frame, allowing the existing native
caption path to recover its complete source. Requirement/Additional are not
locally resized. Search text is player input, not a generated caption.

All four candidate title families:
  job-choice-title forwards native job type, material, subtype, reaction,
    historical-figure and generated-identity fields to the complete job-caption
    switch. RAW reactions copy NAME; generated instrument names/components
    remain open runtime identity inputs.
  color-menu-title:
    Mix {descriptor color} dye (opens menu)
    Tint cloth {descriptor color} (opens menu)
    Tint thread {descriptor color} (opens menu)
    Tint leather {descriptor color} (opens menu)
  material-menu-title:
    {complete material noun} (opens menu)
    The supplier takes native material type/index/category flags. Category
    arms are plant, yarn, cloth, silk, bone, leather, shell, soap, ivory/tooth,
    horn, pearl and wood. Concrete RAW material names and historical-owner
    possessives are dynamic. The call requests noun form, so wood is selected
    instead of the supplier's optional wooden adjective. Missing material is
    unknown material.
  category-menu-title, each followed by ' (opens menu)':
    Weapons and ammunition; Armor; Furniture; Siege equipment;
    Trap components; Other objects; Metal clothing; Engrave memorial slab;
    Mix dye; Dye cloth a specific color; Dye thread a specific color;
    Dye leather a specific color.

Memorial title, native job-caption arm:
  If the figure ID cannot be resolved: Engrave memorial slab.
  Otherwise: {figure identity} (engrave memorial).
  A named figure uses language-name at figure+0x38. An unnamed figure uses
  its unit's native display identity when available, otherwise its creature
  and caste. This is not limited to dwarven personal-name morphology.

Requirement, complete task-availability-and-requirement owner:
  [Requires fuel]
  [Requires ore]
  [Requires ore, fuel]
  [Requires {first unavailable non-preserved reaction reagent}]
The reaction-reagent-description virtual converts raw reagent type/subtype,
material, constraints, reaction classes/products, contained-item and tool-use
fields to the native job-item grammar and capitalizes its first letter.
job-item-requirement, requirement-item-noun, requirement-tool-use and
requirement-material-category retain the complete suppliers and switches.
Independent flags concatenate in native order; their combinations and RAW
identities are open, not a finite screenshot-derived string list.

Additional, complete task-choice-construction and memorial-refresh owners:
  {integer} available
  At least {integer} available
  At least {integer} dye available
  At least {integer} thread/dye available
  At least {integer} cloth/dye available
  At least {integer} leather/dye available
Native displayed counts are retained without division or recomputation.
Memorial status is composed from native state and comma-space separators:
  Ghost; Not memorialized; Entombed; Entombed and memorialized; Memorialized
and one slab state:
  slab engraved; no slabs engraved; {integer} slabs engraved
The refresh producer also stores capitalized Slab engraved / No slabs
engraved. Missing native components are not invented.

pe-raw-name-and-reagent-sources.tsv retains the actual installed RAW source
fields from each configured Windows game, including color descriptors,
reaction names/reagents/products, item, material and creature/caste names.
Generated names and player-authored identities are runtime inputs to their
established identity grammars; they cannot be exhaustively listed as literals.

Upper-left task tooltip, complete native producer and painter grammar:
  The actual reaction category is not the fixed category-menu family. Its
  vtable is 0x16be6e0 in the reference PE and its +0x38 supplier is 0x8c2bf0.
  Construction is inline in task-availability-and-requirement, at the native
  vtable installation 0x8c470a. pe-vtables.tsv retains all slots for this family.
  A category token at candidate+0x48 is matched against the native category
  vector. No match produces no tooltip. A match reads CATEGORY_DESCRIPTION
  at category+0x68 and sends the complete stored paragraph to the 29-column
  splitter. Generated INSTRUMENT_PIECE and INSTRUMENT categories
  use the same path as RAW categories; the spelling is not a special case.

  job-choice +0x38, task-choice-tooltip (0x8c2ca0 / 0x8c0520), emits these
  independent sections in native order:
    nonempty product selector -> Produces: -> one full item caption per product;
    nonempty reagent selector -> Requires: -> one full item caption per reagent;
    job type 0xd1 -> matching reaction token -> its DESCRIPTION vector.
  Each DESCRIPTION entry can supply its own nonempty prose, a USE_TOOL entry
  (type 0x56, matching tool token, tool definition+0x188), or a USE_INSTRUMENT
  entry (type 0xd, matching instrument token, instrument definition+0x278).
  The native producer inserts blank separators between these description
  paragraphs and preceding content. Generated instrument and part descriptions
  are stored values on the same definitions; their full writers are retained
  under data/extracted/instrument-descriptions and share instrument grammar.
  No description branch requires the Produces: or Requires: heading to exist.

  tooltip-job-products (0xd160c0 / 0xd13100) and tooltip-job-reagents
  (0xd09ca0 / 0xd06ce0) retain complete native job selectors, including all
  switch aliases. Their constructed item descriptors go through the existing
  job-item-requirement owner, including dynamic RAW type/subtype/material,
  counts, contained objects, reaction product/classes and tool-use constraints.
  The item formatter emits a number only for count > 1; singular products
  can be one short word. Every product still owns a separate splitter call
  at 0x8c3327 / 0x8c0ba7, without blank separators between adjacent products.
  Field boundaries therefore come from native paragraph calls, not a leading
  number, sentence punctuation or the shared prose capture's minimum length.
  The supplier switches construct item descriptors, not additional fixed prose.
  tooltip-paragraph-splitter (0x8e7310 / 0x8e4b80) delegates to the complete
  tooltip-paragraph-list-splitter (0x8e7440 / 0x8e4cb0). Both paragraph calls
  and the job producer's inlined reagent wrapping use 29 native byte columns.
  This splits the stored source before addst; individual rows are not complete
  translation keys. The native long-word branch inserts a separating space.

  Painter: candidate hover invokes +0x38 into vector 0x18a1768 (reference),
  or the corresponding classic global retained in the native assembly. Hover
  identity changes clear/repopulate it; the painter reads the current vector
  every frame. Nonhovered candidates, empty vectors and insufficient horizontal
  room draw no description. Otherwise the frame has 31 columns, the body has
  29 columns, and height is the native row count plus two border rows. All
  corner/edge/interior tile branches remain in task-choice-render-branch.c.
  Reference / classic native calls:
    row count before height calculation       0x185913 / 0x1858a3
    background/frame tile cursor              0x185a10 / 0x1859a0
    description row addst                     0x185d67 / 0x185cf7
    final temporary string cleanup            0x185d9b / 0x185d2b
  Every category, product, reagent, authored and generated description reaches
  this same complete-vector painter. The bottom border follows the native
  vector length; it is not independently clipped to the screenshot's height.
